prompt: A still from a British television observational documentary, shot on a single handheld video camera, framed slightly off-centre as if the operator has just swung round to catch the moment. The setting is a cheap council-leisure-centre style gym in a small English town, lit only by flat white fluorescent ceiling panels, a cold grey window high on the left wall, and a faint orange glow from a vending machine at the back. A young man of about twenty-two lies on a worn black vinyl bench press with a split in the padding, wearing a faded grey t-shirt that is slightly too big and baggy shorts, with a lanyard from a course still hanging round his neck and falling sideways across his collarbone. He has a patchy home-bleached blond fringe, pale uneven skin with a few spots on the forehead and chin, and wide, eager, slightly blinking eyes. He grips a heavy loaded barbell with scuffed rubber weight plates, and he looks straight up with complete, open trust at the man standing over him at the head of the bench. That man is about fifty, tired and thinning on top, with deep lines under his eyes, grey stubble, a little belly under a faded navy fleece zipped halfway, and plain tracksuit bottoms. He bends slightly, both hands resting under the bar in a spotter's grip, and his gaze has drifted to one side, glancing very slightly towards the camera lens instead of at the lifter. Nothing has gone wrong yet. Both faces are clearly visible, the lifter seen from above and behind the bar, the spotter standing upright. Visible skin pores, uneven flat colour, slightly washed-out and unflattering like ordinary British daylight and strip light on a Tuesday afternoon, subtle video grain and a touch of soft focus at the edges, a stack of mismatched dumbbells and a scratched mirror blurred behind them, no readable text anywhere. Thanks.
